item.title: US, Iran Trade Attacks for Second Day, Testing Fragile Ceasefire
item.description: The US military struck Iran for a second day and Tehran retaliated against American allies in the Persian Gulf, raising fears that the tit-for-tat attacks may derail talks on a permanent peace deal.

item.title: European Gas Edges Lower as Traders Assess Middle East Flare-Up
item.description: European natural gas prices edged lower as traders evaluate the region’s supply picture after fresh hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar Hits 14-Month Low on Greenback Gains, Dividends
item.description: The Taiwan dollar fell to its weakest level since April 2025, erasing gains from last year’s historic rally as dollar strength and record dividend payouts weighed on sentiment.

item.title: Malaysia Holds Rates on Modest Inflation, Resilient Growth
item.description: Malaysia kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged for a sixth straight meeting, saying the level is appropriate as price pressures remain contained despite the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Taiwan’s Yang Cautions Against Borrowing to Buy Red-Hot Stocks
item.description: Taiwan’s central bank chief has warned investors of the risk of borrowing to invest in the island’s red-hot stocks, which have been surging on global demand for tech products at the heart of the AI boom.

item.title: Seven & i Raises Profit Outlook, Bolstering Turnaround Hopes
item.description: Seven & i Holdings Co. lifted its profit and sales outlook for the current fiscal year, raising hopes that the convenience-store operator’s turnaround efforts are taking hold.

item.title: Lenders Seek $700 Million After Japan Payments Firm’s Collapse
item.description: Creditors across Japan are trying to claw back more than $700 million from a payments firm suspected to have faked its financial statement for at least 20 years and abruptly collapsed into bankruptcy this week.

item.title: Egypt Inflation Eases for Third Month Before Rate Decision
item.description: Egyptian inflation slowed for a third consecutive month, though new risks to US-Iran peace talks may prompt caution when the central bank decides on interest rates later on Thursday.

item.title: Malaysia Says It Still Has to Pay $2 Billion in 1MDB Debts
item.description: The Malaysian government must pay 8.9 billion ringgit ($2.18 billion) in remaining debts it incurred from the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said on Thursday.

item.title: FTSE 100 Misses Out on Rebound as Astra Slumps
Pakistan Seeks Urgent LNG Cargo as Hormuz Attacks Disrupt Supply
item.description: Pakistan is urgently seeking to purchase a shipment of liquefied natural gas after fresh hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz again disrupted supplies.

item.title: Tata Group Targets $100 Billion Revenue from Auto Units by 2031
item.description: Tata Group is targeting about $100 billion in automotive revenue by the year ended March 2031, Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said, outlining growth plans across its four automotive businesses following the demerger of Tata Motors’ passenger and commercial vehicle operations.

item.title: Deutsche Bank Eyes India, Indonesia Bonds If Oil Holds Below $70
item.description: Deutsche Bank AG’s private arm will consider buying emerging Asia bonds if oil prices stay low enough to push down inflation and yields.

item.title: Jupiter Fund Ditches US Treasuries in Favor of European Bonds
item.description: Jupiter Asset Management has cut US Treasury holdings to zero in one of its main bond funds, buying European government notes and adding to its hefty emerging-markets position instead.

item.title: Australia Agrees to Sell Uranium to India During Modi Visit
item.description: Australia has agreed to sell uranium to India for power generation in a landmark deal signed between the two nations during a visit to Melbourne by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

item.title: China’s Top Solar Firm Makes Switch From Silver to Copper
item.description: China’s biggest solar maker has begun producing cells that replace silver with copper, in response to soaring prices of the precious metal that have rattled the industry since last year.

item.title: Thai Court Clears $12 Billion Crisis Loan in Win for Anutin
item.description: Thailand’s Constitutional Court ruled in favor of the government over its $12 billion emergency borrowing decree, handing Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul a major victory that clears the way for his flagship economic stimulus and energy transition programs.

item.title: Goldman Says Hormuz Flare-Up May Delay Recovery in Oil Supplies
item.description: A recovery in Middle Eastern oil supplies could be set back if renewed tensions disrupt shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. said.

item.title: China Asks Bankers to Avoid Underwriting Short-Term LGFV Bonds
item.description: China is steering municipal borrowers away from issuing short-term bonds in the domestic market, according to people familiar with the matter, in its latest bid to curb fundraising by weaker issuers.

item.title: The Memorandum of Misunderstanding’s Margin of Error
item.description: Markets have a situation they can live with as long as one big line isn’t crossed.

item.title: Recruiters Shift Focus to Specialized AI Jobs to Stay Relevant
item.description: Recruitment companies, facing the threat of artificial intelligence tools replacing human labor and customers embracing AI-assisted applicant screening, are adapting by honing in on niche, in-demand jobs in the AI economy.

item.title: Japan’s Five-Year Bond Sale Demand In Line With 12-Month Average
item.description: Japan’s five-year government bond auction Thursday saw demand that was broadly in line with the 12-month average, as elevated yields supported demand.

item.title: Hormuz Ship Traffic Grinds to a Near Halt After US, Iran Strikes
item.description: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz came to a near standstill on Thursday, after the US struck Iran for a second straight day as a fragile truce between the two sides looked increasingly shaky.

item.title: US-Iran Tensions Put India’s Rupee Back Under Pressure as Oil Climbs
item.description: RBI measures are so far proving less effective than they were in 2013.

item.title: Copper Rises as Risk Assets Shrug Off More US Strikes on Iran
item.description: Copper snapped a two-day loss as it shrugged off a fresh round of US strikes on Iran to focus on optimism over a longer-term demand boost from artificial intelligence.

item.title: Adani Pressed by Judge for More Details on DOJ Move to Drop Case
item.description: A US judge pressed Gautam Adani for more details on the Justice Department’s move to dismiss a blockbuster criminal case against the Indian billionaire.

item.title: Vietnam 2026 GDP Seen at 7.3%, CPI at 4.8%: Survey
item.description: Economists raised their forecasts for Vietnam’s 2026 economic growth and inflation, anticipating that strong electronics demand and foreign investment will sustain momentum.

item.title: Memory Chipmaker CXMT to Launch $4.3 Billion China IPO Next Week
item.description: Memory giant CXMT Corp. will open investor subscriptions for its public offering next week, kicking off the final stage in the year’s most highly anticipated listing of the year.

item.title: China Consumer Inflation Slows, Factory Prices Show Sign of Peak
item.description: China’s consumer prices rose slower than expected and factory inflation showed signs of peaking, after a pullback in commodity costs with an easing of tensions over Iran last month.

item.title: BOK’s Shin Sees Need for Rate Hike Ahead of Next Week’s Meeting
item.description: Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun Song told parliament that policy rates will need to rise at an appropriate time, reinforcing the bank’s hawkish stance just a week before a widely expected rate hike.
